quick_skim.title: Generative Text Modelling and Language-Guided Visual Attention for Deciphering Palimpsests
quick_skim.abstract: Recovering obscured text in palimpsests, i.e. the manuscripts where the original writing (under-text) was erased and overwritten for reuse, is vital for preserving lost information. Due to the nature of the material, such a task can be highly challenging and time-consuming. This paper presents an approach towards automated palimpsest handwritten text modeling for under-text recovery. We investigate generative models, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and diffusion models, and design a custom denoising diffusion model that learns structured noise patterns to reconstruct the under-text. The recovered text is subsequently processed by a fine-tuned, attention-based handwritten text recognition network. Furthermore, we investigate a language-guided recognition framework that leverages textual class descriptions as informative priors, enabling the text recognition model to distinguish meaningful features from noise. This is achieved by grounding task-specific descriptions, phrased in words or sentences, through visual attention maps generated by pretrained vision-language models like CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training). To facilitate future research and benchmarking, we release new datasets for synthetic palimpsests (currently scarce), CLIP-compatible text descriptions, and pre-trained models with code.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对重写本中被擦除覆盖的底层文字难以恢复的问题，本文提出自动化的重写本手写文本建模方法。方法先比较GAN与扩散模型，设计学习结构化噪声模式的自定义去噪扩散模型重建底层文字，再用微调的注意力手写文本识别网络进行识别。实验表明该流程能有效恢复并识别被覆盖的手写内容。工作将生成式复原与注意力HTR结合，为古籍手写文本识别提供了可复用的技术路线。

quick_skim.title: A Systematic Comparison of Search Space Complexity and Efficiency for Time-Synchronous End-to-End ASR Models
quick_skim.abstract: Search is a central component of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems and has been deeply investigated for classical ASR modeling based on Hidden Markov Models (HMMs). However, in work on current sequence-to-sequence ASR architectures it is often simplified to a small fixed-size beam search without external Language Model (LM). In this work, we present a comparative analysis of search space complexity and efficiency for Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) and neural transducer models under different pruning strategies and LM configurations. We show that these end-to-end (E2E) models work with a small search space most of the time but exhibit large temporary peaks in hypothesis count during periods of uncertainty. Score-based pruning dynamically adapts the search to model uncertainty, leading to a significantly lower Real-Time Factor (RTF). Our results highlight the limitations of search with low fixed-size beam pruning and provide practical guidelines for efficient search in E2E ASR.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: This work compares search space complexity and efficiency of CTC and neural transducer ASR models under different pruning and language model settings, showing end-to-end models mostly use small search spaces but spike during ambiguous periods.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 端到端语音识别中的搜索过程常被简化为固定小规模束搜索，缺乏系统分析。本文针对CTC与神经转导两类模型，在不同剪枝策略和语言模型配置下比较其搜索空间复杂度与效率。实验表明这些模型多数时间只需很小搜索空间，但在歧义时段会出现假设数量的临时高峰。该分析为理解序列到序列解码的计算行为提供了依据。
